_readme: The plain-English layer. `content/` stays the auditable extraction from the trainers' PDFs; this file is
what we add on the way to the learner so a first-week reader is never stuck. Three jobs, one file:
acronyms      — spelled out the first time each level mentions them, in words not more letters.
substitutions — hard formal words replaced by the everyday one, in prose only (never in code).
glossary      — the words that stay, because they ARE the subject, explained in one short line and
shown under the level the learner is reading.
Rules a gate checks (pnpm content:lint): an entry's `plain` is at most 20 words, uses no word from
`substitutions`, and does not hide another acronym inside it. Add a term with one line, not a paragraph.

acronyms.HTML: the markup that names what is on a page
acronyms.CSS: the rules that say how the page looks
acronyms.JSON: plain text that holds data in names and values
acronyms.URL: the web address you type or paste
acronyms.HTTP: the way a browser and a server talk to each other
acronyms.HTTPS: the same talk, scrambled so others cannot read it
acronyms.DNS: the book that turns a name into a number
acronyms.DHCP: the setting that hands out addresses on a network
acronyms.IP: the number that identifies one machine on a network
acronyms.RAM: fast, temporary memory that forgets when power goes off
acronyms.CPU: the chip that runs your instructions, one at a time
acronyms.GPU: a chip built to do many sums at once, for pictures
acronyms.SSD: storage with no moving parts, so it is fast and tough
acronyms.HDD: storage on a spinning disk — cheap, slow, fragile
acronyms.BIOS: the first program a PC runs, before Windows starts
acronyms.UEFI: the newer BIOS, with a mouse and a file browser
acronyms.DOM: the page as a tree the code can reach into
acronyms.API: a door one program uses to ask another for help
acronyms.MFA: a second proof it is you, usually a code on your phone
acronyms.VPN: a private tunnel for your traffic across a public network
acronyms.WAN: a network that joins places far apart
acronyms.VLAN: one cable split into several separate networks
acronyms.ISP: the company that gives you the internet
acronyms.NAT: how one public address serves a whole building
acronyms.SMTP: how mail leaves your server on its way out
acronyms.IMAP: how mail is read from the server, kept in sync
acronyms.KPI: the one number that tells you if it is working
acronyms.SEO: the work that makes a page easier to find in search
acronyms.CTR: how many people click, out of how many see it
acronyms.CPC: what you pay each time someone clicks your ad
acronyms.ROI: what you made back, against what you spent
acronyms.CRM: the book of every customer and what you promised them
acronyms.CMS: a tool to change a site without touching code
acronyms.PNG: a sharp image that can hold clear edges and transparency
acronyms.JPEG: a photo format that shrinks by dropping detail
acronyms.SVG: a picture drawn from shapes, so it stays sharp at any size
acronyms.RGB: colour made from red, green and blue light
acronyms.CMYK: colour mixed from four inks, for printing
acronyms.UI: the parts of a product you touch and see
acronyms.UX: how the whole task feels to the person doing it
acronyms.OS: the program that runs the machine and its apps
acronyms.CPU-usage: how busy the chip is, as a share of what it can do
acronyms.CSV: a table saved as plain text, one line per row
acronyms.PDF: a fixed page, made to be read or printed, not edited
acronyms.USB: the plug nearly every small device uses
acronyms.QR: the square code a phone camera reads
acronyms.WI-FI: networking over radio instead of cable
acronyms.FAQ: the answers page for questions people keep asking
